cards.text: This is a psalm of David, and he opens by calling out to the LORD, his Rock. He's begging God not to be deaf to him. And he's worried about what happens if God stays quiet.

cards.question: David says that if the LORD stays silent, he'll be like whom?

cards.text: Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer waiting for somebody to say ANYTHING. So when David says please don't stay silent? Whew. I FEEL that.

cards.question: David cries out to the LORD for mercy, and he lifts up his hands toward the LORD's holy ___.

cards.text: Then David begs the LORD not to drag him away with the wicked, the workers of iniquity. And these folks have a sneaky move.

cards.question: What's the sneaky move these wicked people pull on their neighbors?

answers.text: They speak peace with malice in their hearts
They lend money and then charge double
They move the boundary stones at night

cards.text: Peace on the outside, malice on the inside. That's a cookie golden on top and RAW in the middle, and friend, I have SERVED that cookie.

cards.question: True or false: David asks the LORD to repay these two-faced people for what their hands have done.

cards.text: Then David says why. These people show no regard for the works of the LORD, or for what His hands have done.

cards.question: Since these wicked people ignore what the LORD's hands have done, what does David say the LORD will do to them?

answers.text: Tear them down and never rebuild them
Send them far away into exile
Turn all their fields into dust

cards.text: And then the whole psalm FLIPS. All that HEAR me, HELP me, DON'T leave me... and now David is blessing the LORD. Same guy. Same psalm. What happened?!

cards.question: True or false: David blesses the LORD because his enemies have finally run off.

cards.text: Then David says the LORD is his strength and his shield. Strength AND a shield? Friend, my whole defense system is a mustache.

cards.question: With the LORD as his strength and his shield, what does David's heart do?
True or false: once David is helped, his heart rejoices and he thanks the LORD with a song.

cards.text: Then David zooms out past himself. The LORD isn't just strong for David.

cards.question: David says the LORD is the strength of His ___.

cards.text: He's also a stronghold of salvation for His anointed. And David closes by asking the LORD to save His people and bless His inheritance.

cards.question: Besides saving and blessing them, what else does David ask the LORD to do for His people?

answers.text: Shepherd them and carry them forever
Gather them into one great city
Give them rest from every war

findings.problem: "he's worried about what happens if God stays quiet" states David's feeling as fact. Verse 1 gives the consequence ("I will be like those descending to the Pit") but never says David is worried. The feeling needs to be marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke reacting to verse 1, which cards 1 and 2 already told. It doesn't carry any new part of the passage, so it works as a recap with a joke instead of a joke riding on a story beat.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact word of the line ("holy ___"). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason between sanctuary, mountain and city, which are all familiar "holy ___" phrases. This tests unseen wording, not meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This story card restates verse 3 ("Peace on the outside, malice on the inside"), which card 6 just answered, and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it's a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "Then David says why" presents verse 5 as David's reason for the request in verse 4. In the text, "Since they show no regard…" is joined to "He will tear them down," not to David's request to repay them. The card adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The recap of David's earlier pleas includes "DON'T leave me," which David never says in verses 1 to 5. His pleas are "be not deaf to me," "Hear my cry," and "Do not drag me away."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The turning point of the psalm is the reason in verse 6: the LORD has heard David's cry for mercy. Card 11 sets it up with "What happened?!", but card 12 only rules out a made-up reason. No card ever tells or asks the real reason, so the baker can leave without the psalm's key detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
